outline: Diabetes mellitus and other disorders of the endocrine pancreas
primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome due to activating GLUD1 variants
mechanism: Activating GLUD1 variants cause hyperactive glutamate dehydrogenase. Increased glutamate oxidation generates ammonia and alpha-ketoglutarate; alpha-ketoglutarate enters the citric acid cycle, increases the ATP-to-ADP ratio in pancreatic beta cells, and stimulates insulin secretion. Leucine allosterically activates glutamate dehydrogenase, explaining protein-triggered hypoglycemia.
vignette: An 11-month-old boy has recurrent episodes of lethargy and diaphoresis shortly after protein-rich meals. During an episode, plasma glucose is low despite an inappropriately elevated insulin concentration and suppressed ketone production. Plasma ammonia is persistently mildly elevated, including when the child is otherwise well. Overnight fasting is usually tolerated better than meals containing large amounts of protein.
lead: A pathogenic variant in which gene most likely explains this patient's disorder?
distractor_notes: ABCC8-related hyperinsulinism can cause inappropriate insulin secretion but the characteristic combination of protein-sensitive hypoglycemia with persistent mild hyperammonemia specifically points to GLUD1.

HADH-related hyperinsulinism can also be leucine-sensitive, but GeneReviews distinguishes it by associated hydroxyglutarate/acylcarnitine abnormalities and does not identify persistent hyperammonemia as its defining feature.
SLC16A1-related hyperinsulinism is classically associated with hypoglycemia after anaerobic exercise rather than persistent hyperammonemia and protein-triggered episodes.
GCK-related hyperinsulinism can produce inappropriate insulin secretion by altering the beta-cell glucose threshold, but persistent mild hyperammonemia with protein sensitivity is the GLUD1 pattern.
key_expl: Protein-triggered hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia together with persistent mild hyperammonemia is characteristic of GLUD1-related hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome. Activating GLUD1 variants increase glutamate dehydrogenase activity; leucine further activates the enzyme, while glutamate oxidation produces ammonia and alpha-ketoglutarate that increases beta-cell ATP and insulin secretion.
objective: Recognize GLUD1-related hyperinsulinism-hyperammonemia syndrome from protein-sensitive hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia and persistent mild hyperammonemia.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Familial male-limited precocious puberty due to constitutively activating LHCGR variants
mechanism: Activating germline LHCGR variants cause ligand-independent signaling through the LH/chorionic-gonadotropin receptor in Leydig cells. Autonomous receptor activity drives testosterone production despite suppressed pituitary gonadotropins, producing gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty in young boys; the phenotype is male-limited and commonly inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
vignette: A 3-year-old boy is evaluated for rapid linear growth, penile enlargement, acne, and pubic hair development. Bone age is advanced. Serum testosterone is markedly elevated, whereas luteinizing hormone and follicle-stimulating hormone remain in the prepubertal range. Serum human chorionic gonadotropin is undetectable, and 17-hydroxyprogesterone is not elevated. His father had similar pubertal changes beginning at age 4; his mother had normal pubertal timing.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains this patient's findings?
distractors: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia due to 21-hydroxylase deficiency
distractor_notes: Central precocious puberty reflects premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis and is associated with pubertal gonadotropin activity; this child has high testosterone with suppressed prepubertal LH and FSH.

21-hydroxylase-deficient congenital adrenal hyperplasia can cause androgen excess, but the normal 17-hydroxyprogesterone and father-to-son pattern with gonadotropin-independent testosterone excess favor familial LHCGR activation.

An hCG-secreting germ-cell tumor can stimulate testicular LH receptors and cause peripheral precocity in boys, but this child's serum hCG is undetectable and the multigenerational male phenotype supports a germline disorder.
McCune-Albright syndrome can cause gonadotropin-independent precocious puberty but is caused by postzygotic GNAS activation and is not inherited in this autosomal-dominant male-limited pattern.
key_expl: Familial male-limited precocious puberty, or testotoxicosis, is caused by activating LHCGR variants that produce autonomous ligand-independent LH/hCG receptor signaling in Leydig cells. Affected boys develop virilization and accelerated growth at an early age with elevated testosterone despite suppressed LH and FSH; the disorder is autosomal dominant but clinically male-limited.
objective: Distinguish familial male-limited precocious puberty from central and other peripheral causes of precocity by recognizing high testosterone with suppressed gonadotropins, negative hCG testing, and a male-limited familial pattern.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Dopa-responsive dystonia due to GCH1 dysfunction
mechanism: GCH1 encodes GTP cyclohydrolase 1, which catalyzes the first of three steps in tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis. Reduced GCH1 activity lowers tetrahydrobiopterin availability, impairing dopamine synthesis and producing childhood-onset dystonia with diurnal fluctuation and marked response to levodopa.
vignette: An 8-year-old girl has progressive inward turning of one foot while walking. The abnormal posture is mild in the morning but becomes pronounced late in the day and improves after sleep. Her mother had similar symptoms as a child. A low dose of levodopa produces a marked sustained improvement. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in GCH1.
lead: Synthesis of which molecule is most directly reduced by this genetic defect?
distractor_notes: GTP cyclohydrolase 1 is not part of the folate pathway; the GCH1 enzyme catalyzes the first step in tetrahydrobiopterin production.
Pyridoxal phosphate is vitamin B6-derived and is not the product of the GCH1 biosynthetic pathway.
Thiamine pyrophosphate is vitamin B1-derived and is not synthesized through GCH1-dependent reactions.
Cobalamin is vitamin B12 and is not the molecule produced through the GCH1 pathway.
key_expl: GCH1 encodes GTP cyclohydrolase 1, the enzyme that catalyzes the first step in synthesis of tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH4 is an essential cofactor in neurotransmitter synthesis, including dopamine production. Reduced BH4 availability explains the dopamine-responsive movement disorder.
objective: Connect GCH1-related dopa-responsive dystonia with impaired tetrahydrobiopterin synthesis and reduced dopamine production.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis due to CSF2RA deficiency
mechanism: CSF2RA encodes the alpha subunit of the GM-CSF receptor. Loss of effective GM-CSF signaling impairs terminal function of alveolar macrophages, particularly surfactant catabolism and clearance, causing intra-alveolar surfactant accumulation and hypoxemic respiratory disease.
vignette: A 6-year-old girl has slowly progressive exertional dyspnea and tachypnea. High-resolution CT shows diffuse ground-glass opacities with interlobular septal thickening. Bronchoalveolar lavage yields milky fluid containing periodic acid-Schiff-positive proteinaceous material. Testing for GM-CSF autoantibodies is negative. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in CSF2RA.
lead: Which cellular function is most directly impaired in this patient?
correct: GM-CSF-dependent surfactant clearance by alveolar macrophages
distractors: Synthesis of pulmonary surfactant by type II pneumocytes
Mucociliary clearance by ciliated airway epithelial cells
Chloride transport by CFTR in airway epithelial cells
Secretion of alpha-1 antitrypsin by hepatocytes
distractor_notes: Type II pneumocytes synthesize and secrete pulmonary surfactant, but hereditary CSF2RA-related pulmonary alveolar proteinosis is caused by impaired GM-CSF-dependent surfactant clearance by alveolar macrophages rather than failure of surfactant synthesis.
Ciliated airway epithelial cells move airway fluid and particles; that process is impaired in primary ciliary dyskinesia, not by loss of the GM-CSF receptor alpha subunit.
CFTR is a plasma-membrane chloride channel in epithelial cells. CSF2RA deficiency instead disrupts GM-CSF signaling in alveolar macrophages and surfactant catabolism.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin is produced by the liver and protects the lung from neutrophil elastase. That pathway is unrelated to the macrophage surfactant-clearance defect caused by CSF2RA variants.
key_expl: Hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis caused by CSF2RA variants reflects defective GM-CSF receptor signaling. GM-CSF is required for normal alveolar macrophage function, including catabolism and clearance of surfactant. Impaired clearance allows surfactant to accumulate within alveoli, producing the characteristic imaging and lavage findings.
objective: Connect CSF2RA-related hereditary pulmonary alveolar proteinosis with impaired GM-CSF-dependent surfactant clearance by alveolar macrophages.

outline: Integumentary disorders (hair and hair follicles, nails, sweat glands, sebaceous glands, oral mucous membranes)
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Pachyonychia congenita due to KRT6A dysfunction
mechanism: KRT6A encodes keratin 6a, which pairs with keratin 16 to assemble keratin intermediate filaments. These intracellular networks provide mechanical strength and resilience to nail, palmoplantar, and oral epithelial cells; pathogenic KRT6A variants disrupt filament assembly and produce friction-induced tissue fragility and hyperkeratosis.
vignette: A 13-year-old girl has had markedly thick, abnormally shaped fingernails and toenails since early childhood. She develops severe painful plantar calluses and recurrent blisters after ordinary walking and has thick white plaques on the oral mucosa. Her mother has similar findings. Genetic testing identifies a pathogenic variant in KRT6A.
lead: Which structural network is most directly disrupted by this mutation?
distractor_notes: KRT6A encodes a keratin protein; keratin 6a pairs with keratin 16 to form intermediate filaments rather than actin microfilaments.
Microtubules are not assembled from keratin 6a. The disease-causing defect described for KRT6A is disruption of the keratin intermediate-filament network.
Type I collagen fibrils are extracellular connective-tissue structures and are not the intracellular keratin network encoded by KRT6A.
Fibrillin-containing microfibrils are extracellular matrix structures and are not formed by keratin 6a.
key_expl: KRT6A encodes keratin 6a, which partners with keratin 16 to form keratin intermediate filaments. These filaments create dense intracellular networks that protect skin and nail cells from friction and mechanical stress. KRT6A variants interfere with filament assembly, producing the nail dystrophy, painful plantar keratoderma, and blistering of pachyonychia congenita.
objective: Connect KRT6A-related pachyonychia congenita with defective keratin intermediate-filament assembly and epithelial mechanical fragility.
